{{history-stub}}

[[阿倍氏|安倍氏]]系土御門家…[[室町時代]]の[[陰陽師]][[安倍有世]]（[[安倍晴明|晴明]]の14代目の子孫）の末裔。安倍氏の長者を代々勤めた。安倍氏は晴明以後も朝廷に代々公家として仕えていたが、室町時代に他の公家同様[[氏]]ではなく家名を称するようになった。（一般的には有世をもって土御門家の初代とするが、実際には室町時代中期以後の南北朝時代の当主[[安倍有宣]]から土御門の家名を名乗ったといわれている）。
[[応仁の乱]]を避けて、数代にわたり[[若狭国]]南部（現在の福井県[[大飯郡]][[おおい町]]）に移住していた。当時の若狭は、東軍の副将をつとめた強大な守護大名[[武田氏#若狭武田氏|武田氏]]の守護国であり庇護に与かるため、都の[[公卿]]たちが多数下向し繁栄していた。[[江戸時代]]初期に家康の命令で完全に京都に戻り、[[征夷大将軍]]宣下の儀式時には祈祷を行った。[[江戸時代]]は御所周辺の公家町ではなく、梅小路に研究所も兼ねた大規模な邸宅を構えた。家格は[[半家 (公家)|半家]]（詳細は祖先にあたる[[阿倍氏#土御門家（室町～明治時代）|阿倍氏]]の項目で解説する）。
== 藤原氏の土御門家 == [[藤原氏]]系土御門家（[[日野流]]）…[[南北朝時代]]の[[柳原資明]]（[[柳原家]]の祖）の子・[[土御門保光|保光]]を祖とする公家。保光と息子[[土御門資家|資家]]は[[権大納言]]に昇った。
だが、[[嘉吉]]元年（[[1441年]]）資家の子[[土御門長淳|長淳]]が[[出家]]して[[唐橋在豊]]の子を[[猶子]]に迎えて家督を譲ろうとしたところ、宗家の[[日野家]]をはじめとする一門の諸家が[[菅原氏]]系の[[唐橋家]]からの猶子に反対したのをきっかけに朝廷の議論は紛糾し、[[室町幕府]]の介入もあり最終的には6ヶ所の所領全てを没収され、[[松木家|中御門家]]・[[洞院家]]など6家に与えられて断絶させられた（『[[建内記]]』嘉吉元年10月2日条）。<!--金井静香『中世公家領の研究』（思文閣出版、199年） ISBN 978-4-7842-0996-5 P106-107 -->

[[華族]]（[[子爵]]） |出身地=[[京都]] |根拠地= |人物= |支流=[[倉橋家]]（[[半家 (公家)|半家]]） }} [[阿倍氏|安倍氏]]系土御門家…[[室町時代]]の[[陰陽師]][[安倍有世]]（[[安倍晴明|晴明]]の14代目の子孫）の末裔。安倍氏の長者を代々勤めた。安倍氏は晴明以後も朝廷に代々公家として仕えていたが、室町時代に他の公家同様[[氏]]ではなく家名を称するようになった。（一般的には有世をもって土御門家の初代とするが、実際には室町時代中期以後の南北朝時代の当主[[安倍有宣]]から土御門の家名を名乗ったといわれている）。 [[応仁の乱]]を避けて、数代にわたり[[若狭国]]南部（現在の[[福井県]][[大飯郡]][[おおい町]]）に移住していた。当時の若狭は、東軍の副将をつとめた強大な守護大名[[武田氏#若狭武田氏|武田氏]]の守護国であり庇護に与かるため、都の[[公卿]]たちが多数下向し繁栄していた。[[江戸時代]]初期に家康の命令で完全に京都に戻り、[[征夷大将軍]]宣下の儀式時には祈祷を行った。[[江戸時代]]は御所周辺の公家町ではなく、梅小路に研究所も兼ねた大規模な邸宅を構えた。家格は[[半家 (公家)|半家]]（詳細は祖先にあたる[[阿倍氏#土御門家（室町～明治時代）|阿倍氏]]の項目で解説する）。

'''土御門家'''（つちみかどけ）は日本の[[朝廷]]に仕えた[[公家]]である。 {{日本の氏族 |家名=土御門家 |家紋名称= |本姓=[[村上源氏]][[久我家]][[庶流]] |家祖=[[土御門定通]] |種別=[[公家]] |出身地=[[山城国]] |根拠地=[[山城国]] |人物= |支流= }} == 土御門家（村上源氏） == [[鎌倉時代]]初期に権勢を振るった[[村上源氏]][[嫡流]]の[[内大臣]][[源通親]]（土御門通親）の子孫。通親の四男内大臣・[[土御門定通]]が祖。定通の孫で[[太政大臣]]に昇った[[土御門定実|定実]]を始め、[[室町時代]]初期まで[[大納言|権大納言]]を輩出したが、室町時代中期に有通が早世し断絶した。 通親の長男[[土御門通宗|通宗]]や六男[[土御門通行|通行]]も土御門を号し、特に通宗は死後[[後嵯峨天皇]]の[[外祖父]]として[[左大臣]]を贈られたが、いずれも鎌倉時代に断絶した。 {{日本の氏族 |家名=土御門家 |家紋名称=蝶 |本姓=[[阿倍氏|安倍氏]][[嫡流]] |家祖=[[安倍有宣]] |種別=[[公家]]（[[半家 (公家)|半家]]）

[[東京都]] |人物= |支流=[[倉橋家]]（[[半家 (公家)|半家]]） }} == 土御門家（安倍姓） == [[室町時代]]の[[陰陽師]][[安倍有世]]（[[安倍晴明|晴明]]の14代目の子孫）の末裔。安倍氏の長者を代々勤めた。安倍氏は晴明以後も朝廷に代々公家として仕えていたが、室町時代に他の公家同様[[本姓]]ではなく家名を称するようになった。一般的には有世をもって土御門家の初代とするが、実際には室町時代中期以後の南北朝時代の当主[[安倍有宣]]から土御門の家名を名乗ったといわれている。 [[応仁の乱]]を避けて、数代にわたり[[若狭国]]南部（現在の[[福井県]][[大飯郡]][[おおい町]]）に移住していた。当時の若狭は、東軍の副将をつとめた強大な守護大名[[武田氏#若狭武田氏|武田氏]]の守護国であり庇護に与かるため、都の[[公卿]]たちが多数下向し繁栄していた。[[江戸時代]]初期に家康の命令で完全に京都に戻り、[[征夷大将軍]]宣下の儀式時には祈祷を行った。[[江戸時代]]は御所周辺の公家町ではなく、梅小路に研究所も兼ねた大規模な邸宅を構えた。家格は[[半家 (公家)|半家]]（詳細は祖先にあたる[[阿倍氏#土御門家（室町～明治時代）|阿倍氏]]の項目で解説する）。 {{日本の氏族 |家名=土御門家 |家紋名称= |本姓=[[藤原北家]][[日野家]]庶流 |家祖=[[土御門保光]] |種別=[[公家]] |出身地=[[山城国]] |根拠地=[[山城国]] |人物= |支流= }} == 土御門家（藤原北家） == [[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]の[[柳原資明]]（[[柳原家]]の祖）の子である[[土御門保光|保光]]を祖とする[[公家]]。保光と息子[[土御門資家|資家]]は[[大納言|権大納言]]に昇った。 だが、[[嘉吉]]元年（[[1441年]]）7月資家の子である[[頭弁]][[土御門長淳|長淳]]が[[出家]]して[[唐橋在豊]]の子を[[猶子]]に迎えて家督を譲ろうとしたところ、[[宗家]]の[[日野家]]をはじめとする一門の諸家が[[菅原氏]]系の[[唐橋家]]からの[[猶子]]に反対したのをきっかけに[[朝廷]]の議論は紛糾して[[室町幕府]]もこれに介入し、最終的には[[後花園天皇]]の勅裁によって6ヶ所の所領全てを没収され、1ヶ所は唐橋在豊の子に与えられ、残り5ヶ所は[[松木家|中御門家]]・[[四辻家]]（ただし、[[洞院家]]と所領交換される）などに5分割に処せられて断絶させられた『[[建内記]]』嘉吉元年7月7日・10月2日・12日条。 == 脚注 == {{reflist}} [[Category:公家]] [[Category:村上源氏|*つちみかとけ]] [[Category:土御門家 (安倍氏)|*]] [[Category:日野家|*つちみかとけ]] {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:つちみかとけ}}

[[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsuchimikado Family}} [[Category:Murakami Genji]] [[Category:Abe Clan]] [[Category:Japanese nobility]] [[Category:Kazoku families]] [[Category:Viscount Kazoku families]] {{draft categories| [[Category:Onmyōji| ]] [[Category:Divination]] [[Category:Esoteric cosmology]] [[Category:Taoism in Japan]] [[Category:Religion in Japan]] [[Category:Pages with unreviewed translations]] [[Category:Tsuchimikado clan]] [[Category:new pages]][[category:original pages]] }} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

[[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family

[[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] {{draft}} {{Promising draft|reason=the high amount of work put into it over a long time, see edit history}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]]
