Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019年7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019th year 7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019th year 7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019th year 7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Tsuchimikado clan]][[en:draft:Tsuchimikado clan]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Tsuchimikado clan|Tsuchimikado clan]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019th year 7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019th year 7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[ja:土御門家]] {{出典の明記|date=2019th year 7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{出典の明記|date=2019th year 7月}} '''Tsuchimikado Family''' (土御門家) refers to two distinct lineages in Japanese history: # A branch of the [[Murakami Genji]]'s [[Koga family]], which became extinct in the [[Muromachi period]]. # The head family of the [[Abe clan]] specializing in [[Onmyōdō]] (陰陽道), later recognized as part of the [[kazoku]] (peerage) with the title of [[viscount]]. == Tsuchimikado Family (Murakami Genji) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). The family's influence waned further in the early [[Shōwa period]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == See also == * [[Murakami Genji]] * [[Abe Clan]] * [[Onmyōdō]] * [[Kazoku]] * [[Viscount]] {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{draft categories| }} [[ceb:Tsuchimikado clan]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Tsuchimikado clan]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Unsorted]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Tsuchimikado clan]] [[Category:Murakami Genji]] [[Category:Abe Clan]] [[Category:Japanese nobility]] [[Category:Kazoku families]] [[Category:Viscount Kazoku families]] [[Category:Onmyōji| ]] [[Category:Divination]] [[Category:Esoteric cosmology]] [[Category:Taoism in Japan]] [[Category:Religion in Japan]] [[Category:Pages with unreviewed translations]] [[Category:Tsuchimikado family (Abe clan)]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[Category:Categories to be overwritten]] [[Category:Old Onmyoji forks]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:S11]] [[Category:Q--q]] [[Category:s11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:completion tier 2]] [[Category:pages which might possibly be incomplete but are most likely complete]] [[Category:I think I cleared all the incomplete or blank pages earlier]] }} [[en:draft:Tsuchimikado clan]] [[ja:土御門家]] [[sn:Tsuchimikado clan]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsuchimikado Family}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsuchimikado clan}}

(Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[Edo period]], they were based in [[Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the rank of viscount (子爵). (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[:en:Murakami Genji|Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[:en:Daijō Daijin|Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its Rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[:en:Emperor Kōgen|Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Yin-Yang Bureau|Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they were based in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the Rank of viscount (子爵). During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[:en:Murakami Genji|Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[:en:Daijō Daijin|Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its Rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[:en:Emperor Kōgen|Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the Rank of viscount (子爵). (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[:en:Murakami Genji|Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[:en:Daijō Daijin|Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its Rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[:en:Emperor Kōgen|Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. The family retained its influence through positions such as [[Yin-Yang Bureau|Onmyōryō]] head, overseeing divination, astronomy, and calendar-making for the imperial court. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they were based in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished. In the [[kazoku]] peerage system, the family was granted the Rank of viscount (子爵). (Branch of the Murakami Genji Koga family) |crest = Unknown.jpg |caption = |origin = [[:en:Murakami Genji|Murakami Genji]] (Branch of Koga Family) |founder = [[Tsuchimikado Sadamichi]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Yamashiro Province]] |notable = |branches = }} This family descended from [[Sadamichi Tsuchimikado]], the fourth son of [[Sadamichi Tōshinaga|Tōshinaga]], a powerful courtier of the Murakami Genji. Sadamichi's grandson [[Tsuchimikado Sadazane]] became the [[:en:Daijō Daijin|Daijō Daijin]] (Chancellor of the Realm). The family maintained its Rank among the [[seigake]] until the early Muromachi period but became extinct with the death of [[Tsuchimikado Arihiro]] in 1452. == Tsuchimikado Family (Abe Clan) == {{Japanese-family |name = Tsuchimikado Family
(Abe Clan) |crest = Ageha inverted.svg |caption = {{ruby|Ageha Butterfly|揚羽蝶}} |origin = [[Abe Clan]] |founder = [[Abe no Seimei]], [[Tsuchimikado Yusada]] |type = [[Kuge]] (Court nobility), [[Kazoku]] (Viscount) |estate = [[Heian-kyō]], [[Nadashō]], and later [[Tokyo]] |notable = [[Tsuchimikado Hisamitsu]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]], [[Tsuchimikado Haruzane]] |branches = [[Kurahashi Family]] (Viscount) }} The Abe clan, claiming descent from [[:en:Emperor Kōgen|Emperor Kōgen]], produced [[Abe no Seimei]], a renowned [[Onmyōdō]] master. During the [[:en:Ōnin War|Ōnin War]], the Tsuchimikado family moved to [[:en:Wakasa Province|Wakasa Province]], where they continued their academic traditions. By the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], they were based in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], holding a stipend of 177 koku. Under [[Tsuchimikado Haruyuki]] during the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] era, the family regained its authority in calendar-making after the collapse of the [[Tokugawa shogunate]]. However, the family lost its traditional roles during the [[Meiji Restoration]] when [[Onmyōdō]] and its related practices were abolished.
